body:
Hello, first-year students. I'm your school counselor,
Hannah Kim. How is your new school life? You may
have experienced a situation (A)[where / which]
things didn't go as you expected at school. Have
you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a
look at the following two cases.
The first case is about a student (B)[naming /
named] Hajun. On the first day of school, Hajun's
homeroom teacher introduced several school clubs.
At that time, Hajun ⓐ___________________. He thought
that any indoor club would be okay since he was
not an outdoor person. Can you guess what happened
on the day of choice? He joined the soccer club.
What made him (C)[choose / to choose] soccer?
Well, a few days before submitting his application,
he heard that the soccer club was so popular that
half of his classmates were applying for it. This
made him think that the soccer club was something
special. With this in mind, he signed up for the
soccer club just because others (D)[were / did].
However, after he had joined the club, he realized
that soccer was not for him. In the end, he
regretted his decision.

윗글의 괄호 (A)~(D)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
(D)
choices: wherenamingchoosedid
whichnamedto choosewere
wherenamedchoosedid
whichnamingto choosewere
wherenamedchoosewere
solution: (A) a situation(상황)을 선행사로 수식하는 완전한 절(things ~ school)이 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 알맞다. (B) ‘하준이라고 이름 지어진 학생’이라는 의미로, 수식하는 a student와 수동의 관계를 이루므로 과거분사 named가 알맞다. (C) 사역동사 made의 목적격보어이므로, 동사원형 choose가 알맞다. (D) 앞에 나온 동사를 반복하지 않기 위해 대동사를 사용할 수 있으며 일반동사의 대동사는 do이므로, 앞에 나온 signed up for the soccer club을 받는 대동사로 did가 알맞다.

body:
When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to (A)[create /
remove] obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people to make excuses for their poor
performances. These excuses prevent the poor result
from (B)[lowering / raising] their self-esteem. This
might work in the short term. However, be careful!
It could lead to repeated (C)[failures / successes] in
certain tasks that you are not confident in doing.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: create  loweringfailures
remove  loweringfailures
create  loweringsuccesses
remove  raisingsuccesses
create  raisingsuccesses
solution: (A) 이러한 유형의 행동을 “자기불구화‘라고 부르며, 자기불구 화는 사람들이 좋지 않은 성과에 대해 변명할 수 있게 한다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 사람들은 과제를 잘 수행할 자신감이 없을 때, 성공에 방해가 되는 장애물을 ’만들‘ 가능성이 높다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 create(만들다)가 알맞다. (B) 이러한 변명들은 좋지 않은 결과가 자존감을 ’낮추는‘ 것을 막아준다는 흐름이 되어야 자연스럽다. 따라서 lowering(낮추 는 것)이 알맞다. (C) 조심하라는 경고 내용 뒤에 이어지므로, 이것은 자신감이 없는 특정 과제에서 반복적인 ’실패‘로 이어질 수 있다는 흐름 이 되어야 한다. 따라서 failures(실패들)가 알맞다.

Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?"
When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower
was very ⓐdifferent from all the other architecture
in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many
local people disliked the tower and complained that
it
would
ⓑenhance
the

Paris.
Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the
tower due to exposure, they became more and
more ⓒfond of it, referring to it as the Tower of
Love. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure
Effect,” is ⓓfound with people, too. Psychologist
Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university

자주 본사람들을 덜 본 사람들보다 더 좋아했다는 사실을 통해알 수 있는 것은 글의 결론으로서 우리는 어떤 것에 더많이 노출될수록 그것을 더 좋게 본다는 내용이 되어야한다. 따라서 ③ ‘우리는 그것을 더 호의적으로 생각한다’가 빈칸에 알맞다.오답① 우리는 그것을 더 바꾸고 싶어 한다② 우리는 그것에 관해 더 궁금해 한다④ 우리는 그것을 더 쓸모없게 여긴다⑤ 우리는 그것에 대해 더 무관심해진다본문변형 the more favorably we view it → the morefavorable we consider it

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people (A)[making / to make] excuses for
their poor performances. These excuses prevent the
poor result from lowering their self-esteem. This
might work in the short term. However, be careful!
It could lead to repeated failures in certain tasks
that you are not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be (B)[because
/ because of] you consider the results more
important than the process. ⓐ_______________________
may ease the pressure to perform well. Accordingly,
you may feel more (C)[encouraging / encouraged]
to try to do the challenging tasks. This can
eventually stop your self-handicapping.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)               (B)               (C)
choices: makingbecauseencouraged
to makebecauseencouraging
makingbecause ofencouraged
to makebecauseencouraged
makingbecause ofencouraging
solution: (A) ‘…가 ~하는 것을 가능하게 하다’의 의미를 갖는 5형식 동 사 enable은 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, to make가 알맞다. (B) you consider the results ~라는 완전한 절이 이어지므로 접속사 because가 알맞다. 구전치사 because of 뒤에는 명사 (구)가 온다. (C) feel의 주격보어로서 주어 you가 ‘격려받는’ 대상이므로 수 동의 관계를 뜻하는 과거분사형 형용사 encouraged가 알맞다.

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people to make excuses for their poor
performances. These excuses prevent the poor result
from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in
the short term. However, be careful! It could lead
to repeated failures in certain tasks that you are
not confident in doing.

you consider the results more important than the
process. Focusing more on the process than the
outcome may ease the pressure to perform well.
Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try
to do the challenging tasks. This can eventually
stop your self-handicapping.
choices: People can excuse themselves for their bad resultsby self-handicapping.
People are inclined to create barriers to successwhen they are not assured of good results.
The reason you are self-handicapping could bethat you value the result over the process.
You can continue to do well in jobs that you arenot confident about by means of self-handicapping.
If the strain of carrying out tasks well is reduced,you may feel more inspired to try to do difficultones.

May 20.
This morning, I woke up to the most annoying
noise. I realized ⓐ[what / that] it was the sound of
cicadas, but I had never heard ones this loud! Then,
I read in the news that every 17 years a special
kind
of
cicada
which
ⓑ[called
/
is
called]
magicicada emerges here in Bloomington, and this
year is the 17th year. These magicicadas spend 17
years underground feeding on roots, and then
come to the surface for a few weeks to reproduce
and die. Now I know why it was the first time I
had heard them so loud. I’m 17.
According to the Internet, depending on the
species and their location, cicadas spend different
amounts of time underground. Most species emerge
annually, but there are others that come out at
longer intervals. The magicicadas in Bloomington
emerge every 17 years, but ones in other regions
can have intervals of 13 or 17 years.
Then, it hit me: 13 and 17 are prime numbers. I
remembered learning in math class that a prime
number is any natural number larger than 1 and
ⓒ[is / was] only divisible by 1 and itself. For
example, the prime numbers below 20 are: 2, 3, 5,
7, 11, 13, 17, and 19. I never imagined that there
are mathematical patterns in nature. I wonder why
magicicadas emerge in intervals of prime numbers.

ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ

thatis called        was
solution: ⓐ 동사 realized의 목적어 자리로, 완전한 절(it was the sound of cicadas)이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. ⓑ that 절에서 주어의 핵심인 선행사 a special kind of cicada를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, ‘call A B(A를 B라 고 부르다)’의 수동태는 ‘A be called B(A가 B라고 불리다)’로 쓰며, 선행사가 B에 해당하는 magicicada라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이 므로, 수동태 is called가 적절하다. ⓒ 동명사 learning의 목적어절인 ‘that a prime number is ~’ 의 주어 a prime number에 이어지는 동사 is와 등위접속사 and로 병렬연결 되어있으며 소수의 정의로 불변의 진리를 나 타내므로 현재시제 is가 적절하다.

emerging in prime number intervals ⓐmaximizes

exposure
to
predators.

predator
populations also have cycles, such as a cycle of
two, three, four, or six years. If magicicadas
followed a non-prime number cycle, for example, a

every 60 years. However, (A)17년 주기를 가진 주기
매미는 주기가 3년인 포식자와 60년마다 한 번씩만

May 24.
After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found studying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals. ⓓAnxious to
solve the mystery, I went to the school garden and
counted the number of petals.
I realized that most flowers have a specific number
of petals. These numbers follow a pattern: 1, 2, 3,

the previous two. This must be the secret Mr.
Johnson was talking about.

I had found the answer. He said he knew I would
figure it out, and he was proud of me. He told me
that this sequence is called the Fibonacci sequence,
named after the mathematician who discovered it.
The number of petals in a Fibonacci sequence has
to do with maximizing the light ⓕabsorption as
plants grow.

After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found ⓐstudying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals. ⓑEagerly to
solve the mystery, I went to the school garden and
counted the number of petals.
I realized that most flowers have a specific number
of petals. These numbers follow a pattern: 1, 2, 3,
5, 8..., and so on, so each one equals the sum of
the previous two. This must be the secret ⓒthat
Mr. Johnson was talking about.
Excited, I ran back to Mr. Johnson and told him
ⓓwhat I had found the answer. He said he knew I
would figure it out, and he was proud of me. He
told me that this sequence is called the Fibonacci
sequence,
which
ⓔwas
named
after
the
mathematician who discovered it. The number of
petals in a Fibonacci sequence has to do with
maximizing the light absorption as plants grow.
Mr. Johnson went on to explain that not only
petals but also seeds form in a manner that
arranges them most efficiently without any gaps. He
showed me sunflowers and how their seeds in the
center bunch up in the middle and spiral out. He

counterclockwise spirals. In bigger sunflowers, the
number of spirals increases to 34 and 55, and for
even bigger ⓕone, 55 and 89. I shouted, “That’s a
Fibonacci sequence, too!” He nodded and said that
this is called a Fibonacci spiral, and flowers can
produce more seeds that way than in a straight
line. I guess flowers can do math!
I must confess that I used ⓖto think mathematics
was just numbers and theories, but after finding the
secret numbers in nature, I’m excited to learn more
about math in real life.

명사절을 이루는 관계대명사 what이 쓰인 것은 적절하다. ⓑ 콤마 뒤로 과거시제의 완전한 절(I went to ~ petals) 이 이어지고 있으므로 종속절을 이루는 부사절 접속사 As와, 주어 I, 1인칭 주어에 수일치하고 주절과 시제 일 치한 과거형 단수 be동사 was가 쓰인 것과 was의 보 어로 형용사 eager가 쓰인 것은 적절하다. 본문변형 수를 결정하는 것은 주변 환경이다 17) ③: 주어진 문장은 ‘더 큰 해바라기에서는 나선형의 숫자가 34개와 55개로 증가하며, 훨씬 더 큰 것에서는 55개와 89개로 증가한다.’라는 뜻으로, 더 작은 크기의 해바라 기의 나선형 수에 대한 설명으로 21개의 시계 방향 나 선형과 34개의 반시계 방향 나선형이 언급된 문장 뒤 와, 글쓴이가 지금까지 언급된 19) ②: (A) 앞 절에서 대부분의 종들은 1년마다 한 번씩 나타 난다고 했고, 다음 문장에서 17년 또는 13년마다 한 번 씩 나타나는 주기매미를 언급하고 있으므로 longer(더 긴)가 알맞다. shorter 더 짧은 (B) 주기매미가 12년의 비소수 주기를 따를 때보다 소 수 주기를 따를 때 60년 동안 포식자를 마주칠 확률이 줄어든다는 내용이 When Dr. Hahn got there, he learned that the
ⓐstaple food in Nigeria was a plant called cassava.
Unfortunately, cassava was defenseless against viral
and bacterial diseases, so it did not ⓑyield much
crop. Knowing this, he decided to develop stronger
cassava ⓒvarieties with higher yields. However, Dr.
Hahn faced a problem: there was not much
information ⓓavailable about cassava. Cassava was

ⓔcash crop. To make matters worse, he had never

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ staple: forming the greatest or most importantpart of something
ⓑ yield: to supply or produce something positivesuch as a profit, an amount of food orinformation
ⓒ variety: a different type of something
ⓓ available: able to be bought or used
ⓔ cash crop: a crop that a farmer grows to liveon rather than to sell
solution: cash crop은 ‘환금 작물(시장에 내다 팔기 위해 재배하는 농작 물)’이라는 뜻이므로 ‘a crop that a farmer grows to live on rather than to sell(농부가 팔기보다는 살아가기 위해 키우는 작물)’은 알맞지 않은 설명이다. ‘a crop grown in order to be sold rather than to be used by the people growing it(재배 하는 사람에게 사용되기보다는 팔리기 위해 재배되는 작물)’과 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

According to the Internet, depending on the
species and their location, cicadas spend different
amounts of time underground. Most species emerge
annually, but there are others that come out at
longer intervals. The magicicadas in Bloomington
emerge every 17 years, but ones in other regions
can have intervals of 13 or 17 years.
Then, it hit me: 13 and 17 are prime numbers. I
remembered learning in math class that a prime
number is any natural number larger than 1 and is
only divisible by 1 and itself. For example, the
prime numbers below 20 are: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17,
and 19. I never imagined that there are mathematical
patterns in nature. I wonder why magicicadas
emerge in intervals of prime numbers.

the reason why prime numbers often appear innature

the reason for magicicadas’ emergence in prime-numberedcycles

trade. Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their

ⓒcolored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe

ⓔwere made with "bleu de Gênes" became known

On beaches and at pools, everyone seems to wear
simple shoes with a band across the top of the
foot and between the big toe and second toe.
Amazingly, they are one of the oldest shoes in
history. Ancient Egyptian paintings show they were
worn around 4,000 B.C. Due to the fact that they
have such a long history, they have different names
all around the world. The Japanese call them zories.
New Zealanders call them jandals, which is a
shortened form of "Japanese sandals." However, in
the USA, these shoes are called "flip-flops.“ Just
walk around in a pair of them, and you can easily
guess why they got this name. The rubber soles hit
the bottom of your feet as you walk, making a
flip-flop, flip-flop sound. The sound became the
name of the shoes, flip-flops.

are being worn by more and more people in
various places around the world. Why don't you
look for other fashion items that have as interesting
name origins as those introduced here?

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were
named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a

structures called coral reefs. Brightly colored coral
reefs provide a beautiful underwater landscape.
However, this is not the only reason they are
valuable.
Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect
both marine life and people living near the sea.
Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of
marine life, such as fish and underwater plants.
Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs,
they are often called “the rainforests of the sea.”
Nearly one quarter of all known marine species
depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide
themselves from predators, find food, reproduce,
and raise their young in coral reefs.

As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. When large waves generated by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
This is why they are sometimes referred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”

printing systems)가 ‘제안된’ 대상이므로 수동 태를 이루도록 proposing을 과거분사 proposed로 고친다. ⓕ 선행사 a way 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌 므로 관계부사 how를 사물의 주격 관계대명사 that이나 which로 고친다. *본문에서는 that이 쓰였음 11) ①: 어법상 어색한 것은 2개(ⓑ, ⓒ)이다. ⓑ Because → Because of (뒤에 명사구(the diversity ~ coral reefs)가 이어지므로 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사가 아닌 (구)전치사가 오도록 구전치사 Because of로 고친다.) ⓒ knowing → known (수식받는 대상인 marine species가 ‘알려진’ 대상으로 know와 marine species가 수동의 관계를 이루므로 과거분사 known으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓓ ‘as far as ~ be concerned’는 ‘~에 관한 한’이라는 뜻의 관용구이다. ⓕ 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지는 why, when, where 등의 관계부사는 선행사가 the reason, the day, the place처 럼 일반적일 때 선행사 없이 쓰일 수 있으며 명사절을 이끌어 be동사의 보어를 이룰 수 있으므로, 선행사 없 이 완전한 절(they ~ the sea”) 앞에 쓰인 이유의 관계 부사 why는 알맞다. 12) ②: (B) allies(동종의 것들) → predators(포식자들), enemies (적들) *본문에서는 predators가 쓰였음 13) A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact that there are forests in the sea : • 조동사 may(~할 수도 있다)와 ‘be unfamiliar with ~(~ 에 친숙하지 않다, ~을 잘 알지 못하다)’ 표현을 활용한다. • ‘추상 명사(구)+동격의 that절’ 구조를 활용해 ‘the fact+that절(~라는 사실)’을 쓴다. • ‘there(유도부사)+be동사+명사(구) 주어(~(들)이 있다)’ 표현을 활용한다. 14) ④: 바다 식목일에는 많은 단체들이 해양 식물을 심거나 더 작은 규모로는 사람들이 해안을 따라 쓰레기를 줍는다 는 내용에 이어지므로, 작은 실천이 해양 생태계 보호 에 큰 기여를 할 수 있다는 뜻이 되는 ④ ‘우리가 하는 작은 환경 활동이 바다를 보존하는 데 큰 물결을 일으 킬 수 있다’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 해양 보존은 더 큰 경제적 이익을 가져올 수 있다 ② 한국 정부는 바다를 보호하기 위해 노력해 왔다 ③ 우리는 해양 종들과 그들이 바다 숲에서 하는 역할 에 대해 배워야 한다 ⑤ 전국적인 캠페인이 없으면 환경 보호에 대한 대중의 인식은 여전히 낮다 15) ⑤: 세계의 많은 산호초가 현재 멸종 위기에 처해 있다는 유엔의 보고와 빠른 조치가 없으면 2050년쯤에는 대부 분의 산호초가 파괴될 것이라는 과학자들의 추정이 이 어지므로, ‘이 수중 보물들’로 지칭된 산호초가 멸종 위 기에 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ⑤ ‘멸종의 위협을 받는’이 적절하다. 오답 ① 생물다양성이 풍부한 ② 끊임없이 진화하고 있는 ③ 연구 대상들 ④ 인기 있는 관광지 16) ②: ⓐ 증가하는 산호초 손실은 전체 해양 생태계의 파괴로 이 어질 수도 있다는 흐름이므로 destruction(파괴)이 알맞다. restoration 복원, 복구 ⓑ 세계의 많은 산호초가 멸종 위기에 처해 있다는 흐 름이므로, 세계에서 가장 큰 호주의 그레이트 배리어 리프의 거의 절반이 사라졌다는 흐름이 되는 disappeared(사라진)가 알맞다. appeared 나타난 ⓒ This로 지칭되는 플라스틱 제품들이 바다에 버려지 는 행위는 산호초와 그곳에 서식하는 생물들에게 피해 를 주는 바이러스와 질병을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이므로 spreads(퍼뜨린다)가 알맞다. prevents 예방한다 17) ③: 주어진 문장은 ‘결과적으로, 산호초는 해안의 땅이 씻겨 나가는 것을 막아서 바다 근처의 마을들을 보호한다.’라 는 뜻으로, 산호초가 자연적인 장벽의 역할을 해서 파 도의 힘이 줄어드는 원인이 됨을 설명한 뒤인 (C)에 들 어가야 한다. 18) ⑤: 산호초를 보호하는 것을 돕기 위해 우리가 취할 수 있 는 조치들로 바다를 오염시키는 미세 플라스틱 조각이 들어 있는 미용 제품과 산호를 손상시키는 특정 화학 물질로 만들어진 자외선 차단제를 사용하지 않는 것, 해변 청소를 돕는 자원봉사를 하는 것, 쓰레기를 재활 용하고 줄이는 것, 사람들에게 산호초에 대한 위협과 산호초를 구하기 위해 취해야 할 행동을 알리는 것을 언급했으므로, 산호초를 보호하는 방법으로 본문에서 제안되지 않은 것은 ⑤ ‘산호 보호 기술에 관한 정보를 다른 사람들과 공유하기’이다. 질문 산호초를 보호하는 방법으로 본문에서 제안되지 않은 것은? 오답 ① 해변 청소 활동에 자원봉사하기 ② 미세 플라스틱 조각이 들어 있는 화장품을 피하기 ③ 산호를 손상하는 화학 성분의 자외선 차단제를 사 용하지 않기 ④ 산호초가 직면한 위협에 대한 인식을 높이기 19) ①: 어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다. ⓒ that lives → that live (주어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌며 선행사가 the other creatures이므로 주격 관계 대명사 that을 쓴 것은 알맞으나, 주격 관계대명사 that 의 선행사가 복수이므로 복수동사 live로 고친다.) ⓕ damaging → damaged (해양 지역이 ‘손상된’ 대상 으로 damage와 ocean areas가 수동의 관계를 이루므 로 과거분사 damaged로 고친다.) 오답 ⓑ contributors 뒤의 to(~에 대한)는 전치사이므로 동 명사 creating이 이끄는 동명사구가 목적어로 쓰였으며, 뒤에 목적어 a healthy marine ecosystem(건강한 해양 생태계)이 있으므로 능동형 동명사 creating은 알맞다. 20) ②: 산호초를 죽게 만드는 다양한 원인들이 있다고 설명한 뒤, However(하지만)에 이어 주요 원인으로 지구 온난 화로 인한 수온 상승을 거론하는 (B), 수온이 30°C 이 상 올라가면 산호초가 죽는다고 설명하고 또 다른 (Another) 심각한 원인으로 플라스틱 쓰레기를 거론하 는 (A), 플라스틱 제품들을 바다에 버리는 행위가 바이 러스와 질병을 퍼뜨려서 산호초와 그곳에 서식하는 생 물들에게 피해를 준다고 설명하는 (C)의 흐름이 자연스 럽다.

simple shoes with a band across the top of the
foot and between the big toe and second toe.

that they have such a long history, they have
(B)[similar / different] names all around the world.
The Japanese call them zories. New Zealanders call

sandals." However, in the USA, these shoes are
called "flip-flops." Just walk around in a pair of them,

The rubber soles hit the bottom of your feet as you

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: latestsimilarsound
oldestdifferentmaterial
oldestdifferentsound
oldestsimilarmaterial
latestsimilarmaterial
solution: (A) 고대 이집트인들이 기원전 4000년경에 착용했으며, 그렇게 오랜 역사를 가지고 있다는 내용이 이어지므로 역사상 가장 오래된 신발 중 하나라는 흐름으로 oldest(가장 오래된)가 알맞다. (B) 일본인들은 zories라고 부르며, 뉴질랜드인들은 jandals라고 부르고, 미국에서는 flip-flops라고 불린다는 내용이 이어지므로, 세계적으로 다양한 이름을 가지고 있다는 흐름으로 different(각 기 다른, 다양한)가 알맞다. (C) 미국에서는 ‘플립플랍(flip-flops)’이라고 부른다고 했으며, 그 이유 에 대한 설명으로 이 신발을 신고 걸을 때 고무 밑창이 발바닥에 부딪혀 플립플랍, 플립플랍 소리를 낸다는 내용에 이어지므로, 그 소리가 신발의 이름이 되었다는 흐름으로 sound(소리)가 알맞다.

Do you know what a jumpsuit is? It is usually a
single item that covers your whole body, even your
arms and legs. It is easy and quick to put on and
to take off. As the name indicates, the jumpsuit
began as clothing for jumping from planes. Later,
designers transformed this functional design into
luxurious women's fashion items seen in fashion
shows around the world. Like the jumpsuit, there
are other fashion items with interesting stories
about how they got their names.
Sneak Up in Sneakers
You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived
from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that
sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they
make little noise when people walk. This allows
people who are wearing (A)them to sneak up on
others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole
of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of
noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing
(B)them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise (C)them.

People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is

The colors you wear are important in creating an
attractive appearance. People can learn which color
clothes are suitable for them by identifying their
personal color, a color that perfectly fits their
individual skin tone. To figure out the most
desirable color scheme for your clothing, you must
first determine if the underlying color in your skin
tone is warm or cool. Try holding an object with a
certain color up to your face in a mirror and
decide which color makes you look best. If your
face looks best with colors of pink, purple, or blue,
you have a cool skin tone. If your face looks best
with warm colors such as yellow, orange, or red,
your skin tone is warm. Generally you will look best
with clothes of similar tones to your personal color.
If a color causes your face to look dull, avoid that
color in your collection of clothes.

Whether they are loose fit or slim fit, most of you
have at least one pair of blue jeans. They were
named "jeans" because they were made of jean, a
sort of tough cotton cloth. The word jean is a
modification of Gênes, the French name of the
Italian city of Genoa. In the 17th and 18th
centuries, Genoa was a major center for trade.
Sailing merchants from Genoa traded their goods
throughout Europe, particularly in England and
France. One of the items that made Genoa famous
was a strong cotton cloth, ideally suited to making
tough work clothes. The cloth was most likely
colored blue. French was widely spoken in Europe
at that time, so the cloth was called "bleu de
Gênes" (the blue of Genoa). This is how the pants
made with "bleu de Gênes" became known as blue
jeans in English.
choices: What kind of fabric were jeans made from?

What was the item that made Genoa famous?
Why was French widely spoken throughout Europein the 17th and 18th centuries?
How did blue jeans get their name in English?

After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found studying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals. (A)[Unwilling /
Eager] to solve the mystery, I went to the school
garden and counted the number of petals.
I realized that most flowers have a specific number
of petals. These numbers follow a pattern: 1, 2, 3,
5, 8..., and so on, so each one equals the sum of
the (B)[subsequent / previous] two. This must be
the secret Mr. Johnson was talking about.

had found the answer. He said he knew I would
figure it out, and he was (C)[proud / ashamed] of
me. He told me that this sequence is called the
Fibonacci sequence, named after the mathematician
who discovered it. The number of petals in a
Fibonacci sequence has to do with maximizing the
light absorption as plants grow.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Coral reefs are crucial ecosystems that protect
both marine life and people living near the sea.
Coral reefs provide shelter to an abundance of
marine life, such as fish and underwater plants.
Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs,
they are often called “the rainforests of the sea.”
Nearly one quarter of all known marine species
depend on coral reefs for survival — they hide
themselves from predators, find food, reproduce,
and raise their young in coral reefs.
As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. When large waves generated by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to treat diseases like cancer.
This is why they are sometimes referred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”

Sneak Up in Sneakers
You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is derived
from the term "to sneak up." Due to the fact that
sneakers' soles are mostly made of rubber, they
make little noise when people walk. This allows
people who are wearing them to sneak up on
others. Before rubber, leather was used for the sole
of shoes. Traditional leather shoes make a lot of
noise, and it is easier to hear the person wearing
them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise them.

You have probably owned a pair of sneakers for
everyday activities or sports. They are a type of
athletic shoe designed specifically to be worn for
physical activities and sports. So, why are they
called sneakers? The name "sneakers" is (A)[altered
to / derived from] the term "to sneak up." Due to
the fact that sneakers' soles are mostly made of
rubber, they make little noise when people walk.
This allows people who are wearing them to
(B)[pick up on / creep up on] others. Before rubber,
leather was used for the sole of shoes. Traditional
leather shoes make a lot of noise, and it is
(C)[easier / harder] to hear the person wearing
them. However, with sneakers, you can quietly
sneak up on your friends and surprise them.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: altered topick up onharder
derived fromcreep up oneasier

solution: (A) 앞에 ‘그렇다면, 그것은 왜 스니커즈라고 불릴까요?(So, why are they called sneakers?)’라는 질문이 화두로 제시되었으며, 뒤에 ‘스니커즈’라고 불리게 된 배경과 관련해 그것을 신고 다 른 사람들에게 몰래 다가갈 수 있다는 내용의 구체적 설명이 이어지므로, ‘스니커즈’라는 이름이 ‘to sneak up(몰래 다가가 다)’이라는 용어에서 유래되었다는 흐름으로 derived from(~에 서 유래된)이 알맞다. (B) 앞에서 스니커즈의 밑창은 고무로 만들어져 있어 사람들이 신고 걸을 때 소리가 거의 나지 않는다고 했으므로, 이것이 그 것을 신은 사람들이 다른 사람들에게 조용히 들키지 않고 다 가갈 수 있게 한다는 흐름으로 creep up on(~에게 몰래 다가 가다)이 알맞다. (C) 전통적인 가죽 신발은 소리가 많이 난다고 했으므로, 그에 대한 결과로 그것을 신은 사람의 소리를 듣기가 더 쉽다는 흐 름으로 easier(더 쉬운)가 알맞다. 천재(조수경) 2과

solution: ⓐ generating → generated (접속사 When 뒤에 완전한 절(large waves ~ toward shore)이 온 것은 알맞으나, 큰 파도가 폭풍에 의해 ‘발생되는’ 대상으로 동사 generate가 수식받는 large waves와 수동의 관계를 이루 므로 과거분사 generated로 고친다.) ⓓ more → the more (more creatures가 그것들(산호초)에 ‘의존하는’ 주체이므로 현 재분사 relying이 이끄는 분사구가 more creatures를 수식한 것은 알맞으나, ‘~하면 할수록 …하다’는 ‘the+비교급 ~, the+ 비교급 …’으로 표현하므로 the more로 고친다.) ⓕ has been disappeared → has disappeared (주어부 half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 핵심 단어 half는 부분을 나타내는 명사로, 전치사 of 뒤에 이어진 단수명 사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 부분도 단수이므로 단수 조동사 has를 쓴 것은 알맞으나, 자동사 disappear는 수동태가 될 수 없으며 과거의 행위가 현재까지 영향을 미치는 일을 나 타내야 하므로 현재완료 능동태 has disappeared로 고친다. 명 사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef와 동격을 이루는 표현인 the world's largest가 이중 쉼표에 의해 삽입되어 있다.)

A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact
that there are forests in the sea, but the sea has
forests, too. Sea forests are formed by marine
plants, and numerous marine animals live there with
them. That is, sea forests are (A)______________________
__________________________ and the leading contributors
to creating a healthy marine ecosystem. However,
uncontrolled human actions and climate change
have threatened marine plants and the other
creatures that
live
on
them. So
the Korean
government designated May 10th every year as
“Marine Gardening Day,” the first in the world. It is
meant to raise awareness of the seriousness of
ocean pollution and the importance of creating sea
forests. Accordingly, (B)많은 단체들이 해양 식물을 심
음으로써 손상된 해양 지역의 생태계를 보호하고 보강
하는 데 기여하고 있다. On a smaller scale, groups
of people pick up trash along the coast on this
day.
It
is
important
to
realize
that
small
environmental activities we do can cause a big
wave to preserve the sea.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: natural filters for ocean waste
sources of food for the future
habitats for underwater creatures
natural buffers against natural disasters
a mysterious world of undiscovered marine life
solution: 바다 숲에는 수많은 해양 동물들이 살고 있다고 한 뒤에 ‘즉’(That is)으로 문장이 시작하므로, 바다 숲은 수중 생물들의 서식지라 는 뜻이 되는 ❸ ‘수중 생물들의 서식지’가 빈칸에 알맞다.

중요하다.) 오답 • 슈아: 예전에는 바닷속에 숲이 있다는 걸 몰랐어 – 그런 것들이 존재한다는 게 놀라워! • 원우: 한국 정부는 해양 오염의 심각성과 바다 숲 조 성의 중요성을 알리기 위해 바다 식목일을 제정했대. • 승관: 우리 동아리도 그날 해변에서 쓰레기를 주울 수 있어. 15) ②: ⓑ contained → containing (avoid의 목적어로 동명사 using을 사용한 것, plastic이 불가산명사로 쓰여 pieces of plastic의 형태로 쓰인 것은 적절하나, 미용 제품이 미세 플라스틱 조각을 ‘포함한’ 주체로 동사 contain이 목적어 tiny pieces of plastic을 가지며 수식받는 명사 구 beauty products와 능동의 관계를 이루므로 현재분 사 containing으로 고친다.) ⓓ cleaning → (to) clean (타동사 clean의 목적어 자리 에 the beach가 온 것은 적절하나, help 뒤에는 to부정 사나 동사원형이 이어지므로 to clean이나 clean으로 고친다.) *본문에서는 clean이 쓰였음 ⓖ taking → to take (‘어떤 -을 ~할지’는 ‘what+명사 (구)+to부정사’로 표현하므로 to take로 고친다. 참고로, ‘의문사(what/where/who/which/when/how)+to부정사’ 는 ‘의문사+주어+should+동사원형’이 전환된 형태이다.) 오답 ⓕ 동사 make의 목적어 자리에 온 가목적어 it과 목적 격보어가 수동 관계이므로, 과거분사 known이 목적격 보어로 쓰였으며, 진목적어로 접속사 that에 완전한 절 (coral reefs are in danger)이 이어졌다. 16) ①: ⓐ generating → generated (접속사 When 뒤에 완전 한 절(large waves ~ toward shore)이 온 것은 알맞으 나, 큰 파도가 폭풍에 의해 ‘발생되는’ 대상으로 동사 generate가 수식받는 large waves와 수동의 관계를 이 루므로 과거분사 generated로 고친다.) ⓓ more → the more (more creatures가 그것들(산호 초)에 ‘의존하는’ 주체이므로 현재분사 relying이 이끄는 분사구가 more creatures를 수식한 것은 알맞으나, ‘~ 하면 할수록 …하다’는 ‘the+비교급 ~, the+비교급 …’으 로 표현하므로 the more로 고친다.) ⓕ has been disappeared → has disappeared (주어부 half of Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 핵심 단어 half 는 부분을 나타내는 명사로, 전치사 of 뒤에 이어진 단 수명사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef의 부분도 단수 이므로 단수조동사 has를 쓴 것은 알맞으나, 자동사 disappear는 수동태가 될 수 없으며 과거의 행위가 현 재까지 영향을 미치는 일을 나타내야 하므로 현재완료 능동태 has disappeared로 고친다. 명사구 Australia's Great Barrier Reef와 동격을 이루는 표현인 the world's largest가 이중 쉼표에 의해 삽입되어 있다.) 오답 ⓒ 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지는 why, when, where 등의 관계부사는 선행사가 the reason, the day, the place처 럼 일반적일 때 선행사를 생략한 채 쓰일 수 있으며 명사절을 이끌어 be동사의 보어를 이룰 수 있으므로, 선행사 없이 완전한 절(they ~ the sea“) 앞에 쓰인 이 유의 관계부사 why는 알맞으며, coral reefs(산호초)를 가리키는 주어 they(그들)가 ‘바다의 구급상자’라고 불 리므로 ‘refer A to as B(A를 B라고 일컫다)’의 수동태 인 ‘A be referred to as B(A는 B라고 일컬어지다)’가 사용되어 are referred to as가 쓰인 것, 빈도부사 sometimes가 be동사 are 뒤에 쓰인 것도 알맞다. 17) ④: nourishing(영양이 있는) → toxic(독성의) 본문변형 ⓐ damaging → harming(해치는 것) ⓑ dangerous → destructive(파괴적인) 18) ③: 바다 숲에는 수많은 해양 동물들이 살고 있다고 한 뒤 에 ‘즉’(That is)으로 문장이 시작하므로, 바다 숲은 수중 생물들의 서식지라는 뜻이 되는 ③ ‘수중 생물들의 서 식지’가 빈칸에 알맞다. 오답 ① 해양 폐기물을 위한 천연 필터 ② 미래를 위한 식량 공급원 ④ 자연재해에 대한 천연 완충 장치 ⑤ 발견되지 않은 해양 생물의 신비로운 세계 19) many organizations contribute to protecting and reinforcing the ecosystem in damaged ocean areas by planting marine plants : ⦁‘contribute to+(동)명사(~에 기여하다)’를 활용한다. ⦁수식받는 명사구 ocean areas가 ‘손상된’ 대상이므로 damage를 수동을 표현하는 과거분사 damaged로 변형해 앞에서 수식한다. ⦁전치사(by)의 목적어로 오는 동사는 –ing(동명사) 형태여 야 하므로 plant를 planting으로 변형한다. 20) ⑤: (A) 산호초를 보호하는 것을 돕기 위해 우리가 취할 수 있는 간단하지만 효과적인 조치들이므로 effective(효과 적인)가 알맞다. ineffective 효과 없는 (B) 미세 플라스틱 조각이 들어 있는 미용 제품 사용을 피해야 하는 이유는 그것들이 바다를 오염시키기 때문 이므로 contaminate(오염시키다)가 알맞다. purify 정화하다 본문변형 pollute → contaminate (C) 산호초가 위험에 처해 있다는 것을 알리라는 흐름 이므로 shown(보이는)이 알맞다. 본문변형 known → shown

These underwater treasures are under threat of
destruction. The more coral reefs become damaged,
the more creatures relying on them will lose their
homes. Thus, the increasing loss of coral reefs
might lead to the destruction of the entire marine
ecosystem. The U.N. reported that many of the
world’s coral reefs are currently endangered. In fact,
nearly half of Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, the
world’s largest, ⓐhas disappeared. If swift action
ⓑis not taken, scientists estimate that most coral
reefs will be destroyed by 2050.
What causes coral reefs ⓒto die? There are
various causes, like destructive fishing techniques,
overpopulation of corals’ natural enemies, and
careless tourism. However, the leading cause is the
rise in water temperature due to global warming.
The ideal temperature range for corals ⓓlive is
20°C to 28°C. When the water temperature rises
above 30°C, coral reefs turn white and eventually
die. Another serious cause is plastic waste. Plastic
products, such as bottles and fishing lines, have
been dumped into the sea. This spreads viruses and
diseases,
ⓔdamaging
coral
reefs
and
their
inhabitants.

A lot of people may be unfamiliar with the fact
that there are forests in the sea, but the sea has
forests, too. Sea forests are formed by marine
plants, and numerous marine animals live there with
them. (A)_________, sea forests are habitats for
underwater creatures and the leading contributors
to creating a healthy marine ecosystem. (B)_________,
uncontrolled human actions and climate change
have threatened marine plants and the other
creatures
that
live on them.
So
the
Korean
government designated May 10th every year as
“Marine Gardening Day,” the first in the world. It is
meant to raise awareness of the seriousness of
ocean pollution and the importance of creating sea
forests. (C)_________, many organizations contribute
to protecting and reinforcing the ecosystem in
damaged ocean areas by planting marine plants. On
a smaller scale, groups of people pick up trash
along the coast on this day. It is important to
realize that small environmental activities we do can
cause a big wave to preserve the sea.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)             (C)
choices: That isHowever      Accordingly
That isThusAs a result
NamelyYetHowever
NeverthelessThusConsequently
NeverthelessHoweverNonetheless
solution: (A) 바다 숲이 수중 생물들의 서식지이자 건강한 해양 생태계 조성의 필수 요소임을 재차 말하고 있으므로, That is(즉, 다시 말해), Namely(즉, 다시 말해)가 적절하다. (B) 바다 숲이 그 중요성에도 불구하고 파괴될 위협에 직면해 있다는 흐름이므로, However(그러나), Yet(그러나)이 적절하다. (C) 바다 숲 조성의 중요성에 대한 인식을 높이기 위한 ‘바다 식목일’에 많은 단체가 그와 관련된 활동을 한다는 흐름이므로, Accordingly(그에 따라), As a result(그 결과), Consequently(결 과적으로)가 적절하다.

body:
Coral reefs are ⓐcrucial ecosystems that protect
both marine life and people living near the sea.
Coral reefs provide shelter to ⓑan abundance of
marine life, such as fish and underwater plants.
Because of the diversity of life found in coral reefs,
they are often called “the rainforests of the sea.”
Nearly one quarter of all known marine species
ⓒdepend on coral reefs for survival — they hide
themselves from predators, find food, reproduce,
and raise their young in coral reefs.
As far as humans are concerned, over half a
billion people rely on coral reefs for safety and
survival. When large waves generated by storms
rush toward shore, coral reefs serve as natural
barriers. The force of the waves is reduced as they
hit the coral reefs. Consequently, they prevent the
land on the shore from washing away and thus
protect towns near the sea. Moreover, reefs are a
source of medicine, and many organisms found in
coral reefs are used to ⓓtreat diseases like cancer.
This is why they are sometimes ⓔreferred to as the
“medicine chests of the sea.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ가 흐름상 나타내는 의미로알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: very important
ⓑ: a lot of
ⓒ: find
ⓓ: cure
ⓔ: called
solution: depend on ~은 ‘~에 의존하다’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로, ‘찾다’ 라는 뜻의 find는 흐름상 알맞지 않다. rely on 등으로 고쳐야 한다.

Here are some simple but effective steps we can
take in order to help protect coral reefs. First, you

(B) 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사로 선행사에 수일치 시켜야 하며, 선행사가 institutions, organizations, or individuals로 복수명사구이므로 복수 동사 contribute 가 알맞다. (C) ‘~하는 것을 돕다, ~하는 데 도움이 되다’의 뜻으로 help 뒤에는 to부정사나 원형 부정사(동사원형)이 와야 하므로, increase가 알맞다. 18) ②: 농부들은 곧 새로운 품종들의 우수성을 깨달았고, 점점 더 많은 농부가 그것들을 재배하기 시작했다는 내용에 이어지며, 뒤에는 그들은 남은 카사바를 판매함으로써 더 많은 돈을 벌 수도 있었다는 내용이 오므로, 새로운 카사바 품종 덕분에 사람들의 굶주림이 해결되었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ② ‘새로운 카사바 덕분에 굶주리는 사람들이 줄어들었다.’가 빈칸에 알맞다. 오답 ① 그러나 일부 농부들은 여전히 그것들을 의심했다. ③ 새로운 품종들은 전통적인 종교 관습의 중심이 되었다. ④ 한 박사의 보급 방법은 농업 과학자들 사이에서 유 명해졌다. ⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 가난한 사람들은 카사바를 살 돈 이 없어서 여전히 배가 고팠다. 19) ⓐ to develop → developing ⓑ which → that : ⓐ ‘~하는 데 시간을 들이다’라는 뜻의 ‘spend+시간 +-ing’ 구문을 이루며 두 개의 -ing가 등위접속사 and로 병렬구조를 이루어야 하므로, to develop을 developing 으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ 완전한 절인 ‘what you do will benefit humanity’가 faith의 구체적 내용에 해당하므로, faith 뒤에 동격절이 ‘that+완전한 절’의 구조로 이어지도록 which를 동격 접 속사 that으로 고쳐야 한다. 20) ④: (A) 한 박사는 나이지리아에 도착해서 그곳의 주식이 카사바라고 불리는 식물이라는 것을 알게 되었는데, 불 행하게도, 카사바는 바이러스성 및 세균성 질병에 대한 방어력이 없었기 때문에 많은 작물을 생산하지 못했다 고 했으므로, vulnerable(취약한)이 알맞다. resistant 저항하는 (B) 한 박사는 카사바에 대해 활용할 수 있는 정보가 많지 않다는 문제에 직면했다고 했으므로, lack(부족)이 알맞다. surplus 과잉 (C) 설상가상으로, 한 박사는 이전에 카사바를 보거나 먹어본 적이 없었다고 했으므로, unfamiliarity(생소함) 가 알맞다. familiarity 친숙함 요약문 나이지리아의 주식인 카사바가 질병에 매우 (A)취약하여 낮은 수확을 야기한다는 것을 알게 된 후, 한 박사는 더 강하고 수확량이 많은 품종을 개발하기 로 결심했다. 하지만 카사바에 대한 이용 가능한 정보 의 (B)부족과 카사바에 대한 자신의 (C)생소함 때문에 그는 어려움을 겪었다.

After the lecture from our school counselor, I
made my own rules in order not to create
obstacles when I study.
(A) By doing these two things, I will know what I
need to do and focus on it. There will be no
more excuses for my performance.
(B) First, I will make a detailed plan for each task.
Then, I will take small steps, one at a time, until
the task is done. Second, I will put my
smartphone on silent mode to focus on my
studies.
(C) More importantly, I will focus on the process
rather than the result.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 학교 상담사의 강의가 끝난 후 공부할 때 장애물을 만들지 않 기 위해 자신만의 규칙을 만들었다는 주어진 글에 이어, 그 규 칙들의 내용을 ‘첫째’와 ‘둘째’를 써서 첫째로, 과제별로 세부 계 획을 세우고 과제가 끝날 때까지 한 번에 하나씩 작은 단계를 밟겠으며, 둘째로, 스마트폰을 무음 상태로 전환하여 공부에 집 중할 것임을 순서대로 밝힌 (B), 앞의 두 규칙을 ‘이 두 가지’로 지칭해 이 두 가지를 통해 자신이 그것, 곧 과제를 해야 하고 집중해야 한다는 것을 알 것이라고 한 뒤 더 이상 자신의 성과 에 대한 변명은 없을 것이라고 말한 (A), (A)에서 말한 내용과 비교를 뜻하는 ‘더 중요하게’를 써서 결과보다는 과정에 집중하 겠다고 말한 (C)로 이어지는 것이 글의 순서로 알맞다.

When people do not have the confidence to
perform tasks well, they are likely to create
obstacles to success. This type of behavior is
referred to as "self-handicapping." Self-handicapping
enables people ⓐmaking excuses for their poor
performances. These excuses prevent the poor result
from lowering their self-esteem. This might work in
the short term. However, be careful! It could lead
ⓑto repeated failures in certain tasks that you are
not confident in doing.
If you are self-handicapping, it might be because
you consider the results more important than the
process. ⓒFocusing more on the process than the
outcome may ease the pressure to perform well.
Accordingly, you may feel more encouraged to try
to do the (A)___________ tasks. This can eventually
stop your self-handicapping.
As
first-year

in

ⓓface sometimes difficult moments. It is not

body:
Hello,
first-year
students.
I'm
your
school
counselor, Hannah Kim. How is your new school
life? You may have experienced a situation where
things didn't go as you expected at school. Have
you ever wondered why this happens? Let's take a
look at the following two cases.
The first case is about a student named Hajun. On
the first day of school, Hajun's homeroom teacher
introduced several school clubs. At that time, Hajun
didn't have a particular preference for any of them.
He thought that any indoor club would be okay
since he was not an outdoor person. Can you
guess what happened on the day of choice? He
joined the soccer club. What made him choose
soccer?
Well, a few days before submitting his application,
he heard that the soccer club was so popular that
half of his classmates were applying for it. This
made him think that the soccer club was something
special. With this in mind, he signed up for the
soccer club just because others did so. However,
after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer
was not for him. In the end, he regretted his
decision. Why do you think this happened?

influence of club activities that are not right forstudents on their relationships with their friends
what homeroom teachers and school counselorsshould do to get students to choose the rightclub for them
differences in personality and disposition betweenthose who prefer indoor clubs and those whoprefer outdoor clubs
solution: 첫 번째 문단에서 학교에서 일이 예상대로 풀리지 않는 상황 이 왜 생기는지 궁금해 한 적이 있느냐고 질문한 뒤 하준이가 자신에게 맞지 않는 축구 동아리에 남들을 따라 가입한 뒤 후 회한 일화를 소개하고, 마지막으로 왜 이런 일이 일어났다고 생각하는지 묻고 있으므로, 하준이가 자신에게 맞지 않는 축구 동아리에 남들을 따라 가입하는 후회스러운 결정을 내리게 된 근본적인 원인에 대한 분석이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 ❷ ‘하준 이가 자신에게 적합하지 않은 축구 동아리에 가입한 이유에 대한 심층 분석’이 바로 뒤에 이어질 내용으로 알맞다.

Well, a few days before submitting his application,
he heard that the soccer club was so popular that
half of his classmates were applying for it. This made
him think that the soccer club was something special.
With this in mind, he signed up for the soccer club
just because others (A)[were / did] so. However,
after he had joined the club, he realized that soccer
was not for him. In the end, he regretted his decision.
Why do you think this happened? Psychologists
say that people tend to engage in certain behaviors
just because others are doing them. Also, people
don't want to (B)[exclude / be excluded] from their
peers. These psychological factors cause people to
follow the crowd, rather than act on their own. This
phenomenon is called the "bandwagon effect."
Following the crowd, of course, does not always
lead to negative consequences, but it can lead to
regret. So, how can you make your own choices?
The first thing is to ⓐ________________________________.
Although it might be different from your friends',
don't be afraid (C)[making / to make] your own
choice. As long as you make the right choice for
you, you will be happy about your decision.

I read in the news that every 17 years a special
kind of cicada (B)[called / is called] magicicada
emerges here in Bloomington, and this year is the
17th year. ㉠이 주기매미는 땅속에서 뿌리를 먹으며

species and their location, cicadas spend different
amounts of time underground. ⓐ The magicicadas
in Bloomington emerge every 17 years, but ones in
other regions can have intervals of 13 or 17 years. ⓑ
Then, it hit me: 13 and 17 are prime numbers. ⓒ
I remembered (C)[learning / to learn] in math class
that a prime number is any natural number larger
than 1 and is only divisible by 1 and itself. ⓓ For
example, the prime numbers below 20 are: 2, 3, 5,
7, 11, 13, 17, and 19. ⓔ I never imagined that there
are mathematical patterns in nature. I wonder why
magicicadas emerge in intervals of prime numbers.

After math class, I told Mr. Johnson about what I
had found ⓐstudying magicicadas, and he was
pleasantly surprised. He smiled and told me I
should look for another of nature’s hidden secrets.
He said the hint was in flower petals.
(A) ⓑExcited, I ran back to Mr. Johnson and told
him I had found the answer.

and so on, so each one equals the sum of the
previous two. This must be the secret Mr.
Johnson was talking about.

garden and counted the number of petals. I

He said he knew I would figure it out, and he was
proud of me. He told me that this sequence is

solution: ‘have you heard of ~?’는 상대방에게 뭔가에 대해 알고 있는 지 물을 때 쓰는 표현으로, 유사한 의미를 갖는 ‘do you know about ~?(~에 대해 알고 있니?)’, ‘are you familiar with ~?(~ 에 친숙하니?)’, ‘have you come across ~?(~을 접한 적이 있 니?)’, ‘do you happen to know ~?(혹시 ~에 대해 알고 있 니?)’등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 그러나 ‘What do you think of ~?’는 상대방에게 누군가나 무언가에 대한 의견이나 평가를 물 을 때 쓰는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘드립 기법에 대해 들어 본 적 있니?’를 ❸ ‘드립 기법에 대해 어떻게 생각하니?’로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life are
quite ⓐtender. An example is Doctor and the Doll,
㉠produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to
be about four or five years old, ㉡being facing the
old man while holding up a doll. The man is
wearing a black suit, and there is a doctor’s bag
under the chair. The girl has already put the doll’s
dress under her arm because she wants to get her
doll ⓑexamined by the doctor. The doctor is going
along with her wish and is ⓒpretending to listen to
the doll’s heart. He is ⓓtreating her and her doll
㉢carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face look like a
worried mother at the hospital? Do you think the
girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is just
playing hospital with the doctor? This work helps us
㉣appreciate the innocence of children. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness ⓔevoke a
feeling of warmth, ㉤bring tender smiles to viewers’
faces.

body:
Let’s move on to the next one. Rockwell also produced
works about the social issues of the times ⓐwhich
he was living. Let’s take a look at this piece. This
was painted in 1964. Along the street ⓑwalking a
little African American girl wearing a pure white
dress and guarded by people wearing armbands. A
tomato, perhaps ⓒthrown at her, is smashed on
the ground while juice stains the wall above. The
redness of the tomato easily captures the viewers’
attention. The title of this work is The Problem We
All Live With. Can you guess ⓓwhat contemporary
issue the artist wanted to describe? It is segregation
and racism in the U.S. This work was inspired by
Ruby Bridges’ historic walk. Ruby was the first
African American child ⓔto enter an elementary
school for white children in New Orleans. The U.S.
Supreme Court ⓕhad just ruled the segregation of
public schools for white and African American
students to be unconstitutional. On her first day of
school, she walked past an angry crowd ⓖbeing
protested her enrollment at the school for white
students. The historical background made this
painting an important symbol of the Civil Rights
Movement in the U.S.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: In 1964, Rockwell produced work about the socialissues in his times, titled ‘The Problem We AllLive With.’
A young African American girl dressed in whitemakes her way, protected by people wearingarmbands.
A crushed tomato lies on the ground, stainingthe wall above, and its red color easily drawsattention.
The Problem We All Live With addresses racialsegregation and was motivated by Ruby Bridges’steps.
After protests against Black students like Rubyattending public schools, the U.S. Supreme Courtruled segregation against the Constitution.
solution: Ruby가 등교하던 첫날, 미국 대법원은 인종 분리가 위헌이라 고 판결한 직후였고, 그녀는 반대하는 군중을 지나 학교에 들 어갔다고 언급하고 있으므로, ❺ ‘Ruby와 같은 흑인 학생들이 공립학교에 다니는 것에 대한 항의 후, 미국 대법원은 인종차 별이 헌법에 반한다고 판결했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

Now, look at The Connoisseur, created in 1962. In
the painting, an abstract art piece (A)[hangs / is
hung] on the wall and a gentleman is looking at it.
The man is painted realistically in Rockwell’s typical
style, but the abstract art piece shows splashes of
paint in a variety of colors. Don’t you think that the
abstract art is quite different from Rockwell’s
realistic works? Let me (B)[explain / to explain] why
he painted it. After World War II, art critics
fascinated by abstract art ⓐ__________________________.
In response, Rockwell decided to paint his own
abstract painting. He used the drip technique,
(C)[that / which] was used by modernist artists at
that time. By combining these different styles in
one art piece, Rockwell highlighted his identity as a
painter as well as an illustrator. In addition, we can
see the man only from the rear. Do you think he
likes or dislikes the abstract painting? Rockwell left
the interpretation of the gentleman’s reaction to us.

work of each theme. I will help you understand the
world of his art better. Come this way.
Many of ⓒhis works about everyday life are quite
tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll, produced
in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be about four
or five years old, is facing the old man while
holding up a doll. ⓓHe is wearing a black suit, and
there is a doctor’s bag under the chair. The girl has
already put the doll’s dress under her arm because
she wants to get her doll examined by the doctor.
ⓔHe is going along with her wish and is pretending
to listen to the doll’s heart. ⓕHe is treating her
and her doll carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face
look like a worried mother at the hospital? Do you
think the girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is
just playing hospital with ⓖhim. ⓗHis work helps
us appreciate the innocence of children. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness evoke a feeling
of warmth, bringing tender smiles to viewers’ faces.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 가리키는 대상이 같은것끼리 짝지어진 것은?

body:
Let’s move on to the next one. Rockwell also
produced works about the social issues of the times
he was living in. Let’s take a look at this piece. This
was painted in 1964. Along the street walks a little
African American girl wearing a pure white dress and
guarded by people wearing armbands. A tomato,
perhaps thrown at her, is smashed on the ground
while juice (A)[spots / polishes] the wall above. The
redness of the tomato easily captures the viewers’
attention. The title of this work is The Problem We All
Live With. Can you guess what contemporary issue the
artist wanted to describe? It is segregation and racism
in the U.S. This work was (B)[deterred / inspired] by
Ruby Bridges’ historic walk. Ruby was the first African
American child to enter an elementary school for white
children in New Orleans. The U.S. Supreme Court had
just ruled the segregation of public schools for white
and African American students to be unconstitutional.
On her first day of school, she walked past an angry
crowd (C)[opposing / supporting] her enrollment at the
school for white students. The historical background
made this painting an important symbol of the Civil
Rights Movement in the U.S.

감소시켰다’가 알맞다. 오답 ② 모든 모더니스트 회화 기법을 거부했다 ③ 예술에서 일러스트레이션의 가치를 의문시했다 ④ 전통 사실주의의 등장을 축하했다 ⑤ Rockwell의 사실주의 스타일을 받아들였다 본문변형 devalued Rockwell’s realistic style → reduced the value of Rockwell’s realistic style 11) ㉠ combined ㉡ the drip technique ㉢ identity 제시문 Rockwell은 그의 예술적 ㉢정체성을 표현하기 위해, 하 나의 작품 안에서 자신의 특징적인 사실주의 스타일과 ㉡드 립 기법을 사용한 그의 시대에 유행한 추상미술을 ㉠결합했다. 12) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘디지털 기술을 사용하는 다양한 형태의 예술이 있다.’라는 뜻으로, For instance(예시로)와 함께 음악, 영화, 전시에 이르기까지 다양한 분야에서 사용되 는 디지털 기술에 대해 구체적으로 설명하는 내용 앞인 (B)에 들어가야 한다. 13) ①: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓗ는 모두 Rockwell을 가리킨다. 오답 ⓓ, ⓔ, ⓕ, ⓖ는 모두 The(the) doctor을 가리킨다. 본문변형 ⓒ Many alone or in a group?

How about you?
B1: Me, too. It’s always better to have friends.
B2: Let’s move on to the next question. Do you
prefer a tightly scheduled trip?
B1: I prefer a loosely scheduled one. Tight schedules
can actually ruin a trip.
B2: I agree. ___________________________________________
B1: Since we have so much in common, you and I
could be great travel mates!
choices: I always let others plan the entire trip for me.
I prefer staying in one place instead of movingaround.
I can have more flexibility with a loose schedule.
I enjoy traveling alone because it gives mepeace of mind.
I think a loose schedule usually causes us tomiss must‑see spots.

body:
Do you enjoy trying delicious and exotic food?
Then, Shilin Night Market in Taipei, Taiwan is for
you! With a history of more than 100 years, it is
the largest and most famous night market in
Taiwan. It is heaven for those who want to try local
street food at an inexpensive price. The fun
atmosphere and huge selection of street food make
it popular with both tourists and residents.
Here are some of our recommendations for you to
try at Shilin Night Market. If you find a long line of
people, ⓐchances are high that it is for ji pai. It is
a seasoned flat piece of fried chicken, ⓑwhich is as
large as your face. The crispiness is out of this
world. Another popular dish is oyster omelet. It is a
mixture of eggs and potato flour, ⓒfilled with fresh
oysters full of juice. Sweet sauce poured on top
adds a fantastic flavor. Wouldn’t you like something
to drink now? We recommend some papaya milk
juice. This sweet fruit juice will refresh you and
boost your energy for night shopping. You should
get to the market at around 7 to 8 p.m., ⓓwhen
everything is set up. ⓔWith many people coming
and going, the atmosphere of the market reaches
its peak.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Cultural Festivities and Traditional NighttimeCelebrations in Taipei
Shilin Night Market: Its Role in PreservingTaiwanese Traditions
The Historical Origins and Global Recognition ofShilin Night Market
The Transformation of Shilin Night Market overa Century
Taiwan’s Shilin Night Market: A Paradise forFoodies
solution: 100년 이상의 역사를 지니며 대만에서 가장 크고 유명한 타이 페이 스린 야시장은 다양한 현지 길거리 음식을 저렴하게 즐 길 수 있는 곳이라고 소개하며 대표적인 먹거리들을 소개하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ❺ ‘대만의 스린 야시장: 미식가들을 위한 천국’이 알맞다.

TYPE A. Festival Lover
If you are into spectacular festivals, how about Loi
Krathong in Sukhothai, Thailand? Visit this famous
festival of lights and ⓐjoin the Thai people at a
river’s edge. There, you can release floating lanterns
called krathongs while ⓑmaking a wish. This lets
you release all your negative energy and welcome
good fortune in the coming year. The legend says
that if the lantern remains lit until it ⓒwill
disappear from sight, your wish will come true.
Although
Loi
Krathong
ⓓis
held
throughout
Thailand, Sukhothai is the best because it is its
birthplace.
Sukhothai
also
holds
the
biggest
celebration in Thailand, ⓔwhich lasts for about five
days. In addition to floating lanterns, you can also
enjoy beautiful fireworks, learn folk dances, and
watch spectacular light and sound shows. We
cannot emphasize enough how ⓕbeautifully the
temples and monuments surrounded by bright

the full moon of the 12th month in the Thai lunar
calendar. This usually comes in November in the
solar calendar. However, ⓖsince the exact date

body:
Sustainable travel means finding a way that
tourism can (A)[be maintained / maintain] without
harming natural and cultural environments. Travelers
need to be more aware of the pollution caused by
travel and how that affects nature. ⓐ_____________,
they need to be aware of how tourism affects local
people and businesses. The concept of sustainability
has three key factors. First, the environmental factor
focuses on (B)[reduction / reducing] the negative
impact on the natural environment caused by
traveling. This includes minimizing pollution from air
travel, water use, and plastic waste, and not
disturbing wild animals. Second, the social factor is
about the impact on local people. This includes
preserving and supporting communities of local
inhabitants so that they do not suffer from tourism.
Travelers should respect local customs and traditions
and (C)[adjust / adjusting] accordingly, such as by
wearing proper clothes in religious sites. Lastly, the
economic factor is about using money to positively
contribute to the local economy. ⓑ_____________, by
booking a local tour guide or staying in local guest
houses, tourists can support local businesses.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: be maintainedreductionadjust
maintainreductionadjusting
be maintainedreducingadjusting
maintainreducingadjust
be maintainedreducingadjust
solution: (A) 관계부사 that이 이끄는 절의 주어 tourism이 ‘유지되는’ 대 상이므로, 조동사 can 뒤에 동사원형으로 시작하는 수동태(be p.p.)인 be maintained가 적절하다. (B) 전치사 on의 목적어로 명사(구)나 동명사(구)가 올 수 있으 나, 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 the negative impact가 이어지므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사 reducing이 적절하다. (C) 조동사 should에 연결된 동사원형 respect와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 동사원형 adjust가 적절하다.

Sustainable travel means finding a way that
tourism can (A)[be maintained / maintain] without
harming natural and cultural environments. Travelers
need to be more aware of the pollution caused by
travel and how that affects nature. ⓐ_____________,
they need to be aware of how tourism affects local
people and businesses. The concept of sustainability
has three key factors. First, the environmental factor
focuses on (B)[reduction / reducing] the negative
impact on the natural environment caused by
traveling. This includes minimizing pollution from air
travel, water use, and plastic waste, and not
disturbing wild animals. Second, the social factor is
about the impact on local people. This includes
preserving and supporting communities of local
inhabitants so that they do not suffer from tourism.
Travelers should respect local customs and traditions
and (C)[adjust / adjusting] accordingly, such as by
wearing proper clothes in religious sites. Lastly, the
economic factor is about using money to positively
contribute to the local economy. ⓑ_____________, by
booking a local tour guide or staying in local guest
houses, tourists can support local businesses.

choices: There is no doubt that it’ll be challenging.

solution: ‘It’s[It is] certain that ~‘은 ’~라는 것이 확실하다’라는 의미로 확신에 가까운 높은 가능성을 나타낼 때 사용하는 표현이며, 유사한 의미의 표현인 ’I’m sure that ~(나는 ~라는 것을 확신 해)‘, ’It’s clear that ~(~라는 것은 분명해)‘, ’There is no doubt[question] that ~(~라는 것에는 의심의 여지가 없어)‘, ’It’s obvious[evident] that ~(~라는 것은 명백해)‘ 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있으나, ’It is unlikely that ~‘은 ’~할 것 같지 않다‘라는 뜻으로 가능성이 낮은 일을 나타내는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘그것이 어려울 것이라는 것은 확실합니다.’를 ❷ ‘그것은 어려 울 것 같지 않습니다.’로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

The fourth invention is the wireless headset. It was
devised after an ⓐunexpected incident NASA had
experienced.
The
second
manned
spacecraft
launched by the U.S. completed its mission and
successfully landed in the Atlantic Ocean. The
command pilot was waiting for the recovery team
that would get him and the capsule from the
ocean.
Everything was going smoothly until unexpectedly,
the capsule started to ⓑleak. Water flooded into
the cabin before the team arrived, and the pilot
had to escape, abandoning all of the spacecraft’s
radio communications equipment. This prevented
him from ⓒcutting off the recovery team. He was
left floating in the ocean until he succeeded in
ⓓvisibly getting the rescue helicopter’s attention.
After this accident, NASA and a partner company
developed helmets equipped with a radio system
that could communicate with a designated base
station. Later, wireless headsets ⓔusing this system
were introduced to the world. These days, Bluetooth
technology has been incorporated into wireless
headsets. Now we can connect headsets wirelessly
with mobile digital devices such as smartphones
and laptops.

body:
The fourth invention is the wireless headset. It was
devised after an unexpected incident NASA had
experienced. The second manned spacecraft launched
by the U.S. completed its mission and successfully
landed in the Atlantic Ocean. The command pilot
was waiting for the recovery team that would get
him and the capsule from the ocean.
Everything was going smoothly until unexpectedly,
the capsule started to leak. Water flooded into the
cabin before the team arrived, and the pilot had to
escape, (A)[protecting / abandoning] all of the
spacecraft’s radio communications equipment. This
prevented him from communicating with the recovery
team. He was left floating in the ocean until he
succeeded in visibly getting the rescue helicopter’s
attention. After this accident, NASA and a partner
company developed helmets equipped with a radio
system that could communicate with a designated
base station. Later, wireless headsets using this
system were introduced to the world. These days,
Bluetooth technology has been (B)[incorporated into /
separated from] wireless headsets. Now we can
connect
headsets
wirelessly
with
mobile
digital
devices such as smartphones and laptops.
In our daily lives, there are many other inventions
that have their origins in space technology including
the smartphone camera and the computer mouse.
Private firms as well as government organizations
have invested heavily in space technology for space
exploration. Therefore, we can expect that our
future lives will be (C)[less / significantly] influenced
by space technology that has not yet been invented.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: protectingincorporated intoless
protectingseparated fromsignificantly
abandoningincorporated intosignificantly
abandoningseparated fromsignificantly
abandoningincorporated intoless
solution: (A) 구조팀이 도착하기 전에 조종실로 물이 들어와 조종사는 우주선의 통신 장비를 버리고 탈출해야 했고, 회수팀과 연락할 수 없었다는 흐름으로 abandoning(버리면서)이 알맞다. (B) 요즘에는 블루투스 기술이 무선 헤드셋에 통합되어 스마트폰 이나 노트북과 같은 이동형 디지털 장치에 헤드셋을 무선으로 연결 할 수 있다는 흐름으로 incorporated into(~로 통합된)가 알맞다. (C) 정부와 민간 기업 모두 우주 기술에 엄청난 투자를 해 왔기 때 문에, 미래 삶은 아직 발명되지 않은 새로운 우주 기술의 영향을 크게 받을 것이라는 흐름으로 significantly(크게, 상당히)가 알맞다.

body:
Welcome
everyone
to
the
Norman
Rockwell
exhibition. My name is Harris Clark, and I will be
your guide today. Rockwell is one of the most
famous American press ⓐillustrators and painters of
all time. He produced hundreds of covers for
magazines. The main themes of his art include everyday
life, social issues, and his identity as an artist.
Today, we will take a look at the representative
work of each theme. I will help you understand the
world of his art better. Come this way.
Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life ⓑis
quite tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll,
produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be
about four or five years old, is facing the old man
while ⓒholding up a doll. The man is wearing a
black suit, and there is a doctor’s bag under the
chair. The girl ⓓhas already put the doll’s dress
under her arm because she wants to get her doll
examined by the doctor. The doctor is going along
with her wish and is pretending to listen to the
doll’s heart. He is treating her and her doll
carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face look like a
worried mother at the hospital? Do you think the
girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is just
playing hospital with the doctor? This work helps us
ⓔappreciate the innocence of children. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness evoke a feeling
of warmth, bringing tender smiles to viewers’ faces.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓑ is → are 주어부 ‘Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life‘의 동 사 자리로, 주어부의 핵은 Rockwell’s works이므로 is를 복수동 사로 수일치 시킨 are로 고친다.

Let’s move on to the next one. Also, ㉠____________
____________________________________________________. Let’s
take a look at this piece. This was painted in 1964.
Along the street walks a little African American girl
wearing a pure white dress and (A)[guarded / guarding]
by people wearing armbands. A tomato, perhaps thrown
at her, is smashed on the ground while juice stains the
wall above. The redness of the tomato easily captures
the viewers’ attention. The title of this work is The
Problem We All Live With. Can you guess (B)[how /
what] contemporary issue the artist wanted to describe?
It is segregation and racism in the U.S. This work was
inspired by Ruby Bridges’ historic walk. Ruby was the
first African American child to enter an elementary
school for white children in New Orleans. The U.S.
Supreme Court had just ruled the segregation of public
schools for white and African American students to be
unconstitutional. On her first day of school, she walked
past an angry crowd (C)[was protesting / protesting]
her enrollment at the school for white students. The
historical background made this painting an important
symbol of the Civil Rights Movement in the U.S.

solution: (A) 장소의 부사구 Along the street가 문두에 와서 주어와 동 사(walks)가 도치를 이루고 있는 완전한 절에 이어지는 분사자 리로, 주어인 ‘a little African American girl’ 을 수식하는 현재분 사 wearing과 등위접속사 and로 연결되는 분사로 주어가 ‘보호 를 받는’의 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 guarded가 적절하다. (B) Can you guess에 이어지는 간접의문문을 이루는 명사절로, 명사구 contemporary issue와 함께 의문사구를 이뤄야 하므로, 명사구를 수식하는 의문형용사 what이 적절하다. (C) 완전한 절(she walked past an angry crowd)에 이어 접속사 없이 동사가 바로 올 수 없으므로 분사 자리이다. 따라서 수식받 는 an angry crowd가 ‘항의하는’의 주체로 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사 protesting이 적절하다.

Now, look at The Connoisseur, created in 1962. In
the painting, an abstract art piece is hung on the
wall and a gentleman is looking at it. The man is
painted realistically in Rockwell’s typical style, but
the abstract art piece shows splashes of paint in a
variety of colors. Don’t you think that the abstract
art is quite different from Rockwell’s realistic works?
Let me explain why he painted it. After World War
II, art critics fascinated by abstract art devalued
Rockwell’s realistic style. In response, Rockwell
decided to paint his own abstract painting. He used
the drip technique, which was used by modernist
artists at that time. By combining these different
styles in one art piece, Rockwell highlighted his
identity as a painter as well as an illustrator. In
addition, we can see the man only from the rear.
Do you think he likes or dislikes the abstract
painting? Rockwell left the interpretation of the
gentleman’s reaction to us.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

How did art critics view Rockwell’s realistic styleafter World War II?
What painting technique did Rockwell use forhis own abstract artwork?

What is the gentleman’s opinion about the abstractpainting in The Connoisseur?

(C) This was painted in 1964. Along the street walks

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

Now, look at The Connoisseur, created in 1962. In
the painting, an abstract art piece is hung on the
wall and a gentleman is looking at it. The man is
painted realistically in Rockwell’s typical style, but
the abstract art piece shows splashes of paint in a
variety of colors. Don’t you think that the abstract
art is quite different from Rockwell’s realistic works?
Let me explain why he painted it. After World War
II, art critics fascinated by abstract art devalued
Rockwell’s realistic style. In response, Rockwell
decided to paint his own abstract painting. He used
the drip technique, which was used by modernist
artists at that time. By combining these different
styles in one art piece, Rockwell highlighted his
identity as a painter as well as an illustrator. In
addition, we can see the man only from the rear.
Do you think he likes or dislikes the abstract
painting? Rockwell ____________________________________.
choices: used this painting only to practice the drip technique
painted the man’s expression in detail to showhis reaction
emphasized only the abstract art and ignored thegentleman
left the interpretation of the gentleman’s reaction tous
wanted to convince viewers that abstract art wasmeaningless
solution: Rockwell은 추상 예술에 매료된 예술 비평가들에 의해 자신의 사실적인 화풍이 평가 절하 당하자, 그에 대한 응답으로 현실 적인 화풍으로 그려진 한 신사가 드립 기법의 추상화를 보고 있는 ‘감정가’를 그렸고, 그 그림에서 우리는 그 신사[남자]의 뒷모습만 볼 수 있다고 언급되어 있으므로, 그의 표정을 볼 수 없기에 그림 속의 ‘그 남자가 그 추상화를 좋아하는 것 같은가 요, 아니면 싫어하는 것 같은가요?’에 대한 답을 정확히 알 수 없고 사람마다 다를 수 있음을 유추할 수 있다. 따라서 빈칸에 는 ❹ ‘그 신사의 반응에 대한 해석을 우리에게 남겨 놓았다’ 가 알맞다.

In a broad sense, digital art refers to any type of
art ⓐthat is created and displayed with the aid of
digital devices. This artistic format emerged with the
evolutionary progress in digital media and computers
a few decades ago. In many ways, artworks created
with digital technology sharply contrast with ⓑthose
made entirely with conventional methods. However,
they are similar in that digital art also evokes
emotional reactions in viewers. From this perspective,
ⓒit can be said that digital art has expanded the
territory of art. ⓓThere are many types of art that

solution: ‘It is said that 주어+동사 ~‘ 구문은 ’주어+be동사+said+to부 정사 ~‘로 바꿔 쓸 수 있는데, 이때 주절의 시제보다 종속절의 시제가 앞서거나, 종속절에 완료시제가 사용되었을 때 완료형 부정사(to have+과거분사)를 사용한다. 따라서 ‘digital art can be said to have expanded the territory of art’로 고쳐야 한다. 천재(조수경) 2과

Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life are
quite tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll,
produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be
about four or five years old, is facing the old man
while holding up a doll. The man is wearing a
black suit, and there is a doctor’s bag under the
chair. The girl has already put the doll’s dress
under her arm because she wants to get her doll
examined by the doctor. The doctor is going along
with her wish and is pretending to listen to the
doll’s heart. He is treating her and her doll
carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face look like a
worried mother at the hospital? Do you think the
girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is just
playing hospital with the doctor? This work helps us
appreciate the innocence of children. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness evoke a feeling
of warmth, ____________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: eliciting warm smiles from viewers
highlighting the harsh realities of life
provoking a sense of unease and tension
emphasizing the complexity of human emotions
turning childhood imagination and fantasy intoreality

Welcome everyone to the Norman Rockwell exhibition.
My name is Harris Clark, and I will be your guide
today. Rockwell is one of the most famous American
press illustrators and painters of all time. He produced
ⓐhundreds of covers for magazines. The main themes
of his art include everyday life, social issues, and his
identity as an artist. Today, we will take a look at the
representative work of ⓑeach theme. I will help you
understand the world of his art better. Come this way.
Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life are
quite tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll,
produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be
about four or five years old, is facing the old man
while holding up a doll. The man is wearing a black
suit, and there is a doctor’s bag under the chair. The
girl has already put the doll’s dress under her arm
because she wants to get her doll ⓒto examine by the
doctor. The doctor is going along with her wish and is
pretending to listen to the doll’s heart. He is treating her
and her doll carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face look
like a ⓓworried mother at the hospital? Do you think
ⓔthat the girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is
just playing hospital with the doctor? This work helps
us ⓕappreciate the innocence of children. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness evoke a feeling of
warmth, ⓖbrought tender smiles to viewers’ faces.

윗글의 두 번째 단락의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the importance of play in child development
how children express empathy through imaginativeplay
how Rockwell’s childhood influenced his choice ofpainting subjects
methods used to create a warm atmosphere in Doctorand the Doll
the pure heart of a girl and the gentle care ofa doctor in Doctor and the Doll

환대하는 군중을 마주했고, 이 작품은 미국 인권 운동의 중요한 상징이 되었어.’는 일치하지 않는 내용 이다. 제시문 선생님: 다음 작품을 살펴보자. ⓐRockwell은 그의 그림 들에서 사회적 문제도 다루었어. 학생: 예시를 보여주실 수 있나요? 선생님: 물론이지. ⓑ1964년에 그려진 이 작품은 어린 아프리카계 미국인 소녀가 흰 드레스를 입은 거리를 걷고 있으며, 팔에 완장을 찬 어른들과 동반하고 있는 것을 그렸어. 학생: 바닥에 뭔가 보여요. 저게 뭐죠? 선생님: 저건 아마 그녀에게 던져진 토마토일 거야. ⓒ밝 은 빨간색이 바로 관람객의 시선을 끌고 있어. 이 그림 의 제목은 ‘The Problem We All Live With’야. 학생: Rockwell은 무엇을 강조하고 싶었던 거죠? 선생님: 그는 미국의 분리 정책과 인종 차별을 보여주 고 싶었어. ⓓ이 그림은 뉴올리언스의 백인 초등학교에 다니고 있는 아프리카계 미국인 아이인 Ruby Bridges 에 의해 영감을 받았어. 학생: 그녀는 정말 용감했겠네요. 선생님: 맞아. ⓔ그녀는 학교에 가는 길에 환대하는(→ 적대적인) 군중을 마주했고, 이 작품은 미국 인권 운동 의 중요한 상징이 되었어. 18) ③: perspective는 ‘관점’이라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나 ‘그들이 크 기와 위치에서 현실적으로 보이도록 3차원 물체를 2차 원 표면에  표현하는 기술’은 perspective의 또 다른 뜻 인 ‘원근법’에 대한 영영풀이이므로, ‘a particular way of thinking about or considering something (어떤 것 을 생각하거나 고려하는 특정한 방식)’과 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다. 오답 ⓐ 나타나다: 숨겨져 있은 후 보이게 되거나 알려지다 ⓑ 전통적인: 새롭거나 독창적이지 않은, 일반적이거나 전통적인 방식과 방법을 따르는 ⓓ 전시회: 사람들이 볼 수 있도록 예술, 물건들, 정보 의 공개적인 전시 ⓔ 포함하다: 무언가를 전체의 일부로 포함하거나 다른 것과 그것을 결합하다 19) ⑤: 음악, 영화, 미술관 전시 등 다양한 예술이 디지털 기술 을 활용해 창작되고 편집되며, 전시와 감상을 통해 관 람자에게 전달된다는 흐름으로, 빈칸에는 ⑤ ‘예술의 영 역을 넓혔다’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 첨단 컴퓨터 프로그램으로만 제작될 수 있다 ② 모든 예술 장르의 경계를 없앴다 ③ 물리적인 미술관의 필요성을 없앴다 ④ 전통 미술보다 감정적으로 더 강력하다 20) ④: 디지털 아트는 디지털 기기를 활용해 제작되고 전시되 는 모든 형태의 예술을 가리키는데, 전통 예술과 방식 은 다르지만 유사하게 사람들에게 감정을 불러일으키 고, 음악, 영화, 미술관 전시 등 다양한 분야에서 디지 털 기술이 활용된다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 요지로 ④ ‘디지털 아트는 감정을 불러일으킬 수 있고, 다양한 분야에서 사용된다.’가 알맞다. 오답 ① 디지털 아트와 전통 예술은 공존할 수 없다. ② 디지털 아트는 모든 면에서 전통 예술보다 우수하다. ③ 디지털 아트는 대부분의 관람자가 감상하기에는 너 무 복잡하다. ⑤ 디지털 아트는 가상공간에서만 존재할 수 있으며 현실 세계 전시에서는 아니다.

food was vital for survival in space. In order to get

spacecraft. However, there was a major obstacle.

accelerates the aging of plants and the decaying of

clean air (A)[during / while] in space, scientists

(B) 접속사 once(일단 ~하면)가 이끄는 절의 주어 harmful bacteria가 ‘제거되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어지는 목적어가 없으므 로 과거시제 수동태(be동사+p.p.) were removed가 적절하다. The fourth invention is the wireless headset. It was
devised after an unexpected incident NASA had
experienced. The second manned spacecraft launched
by the U.S. completed its mission and successfully
landed in the Atlantic Ocean. The command pilot
was waiting for the recovery team that would get
him and the capsule from the ocean.
Everything was going smoothly until unexpectedly,
the capsule started to leak. Water flooded into the
cabin before the team arrived, and the pilot had to
escape, abandoning all of the spacecraft’s radio
communications equipment. This prevented him
from communicating with the recovery team. He
was left floating in the ocean until he succeeded in
visibly getting the rescue helicopter’s attention. After
this
accident,
NASA
and
a
partner
company
developed helmets equipped with a radio system
that could communicate with a designated base
station. Later, wireless headsets using this system
were introduced to the world. These days, Bluetooth
technology has been incorporated into wireless
headsets. Now we can connect headsets wirelessly
with mobile digital devices such as smartphones
and laptops.
choices: What incident led to the development of thewireless headset?
Why was the pilot unable to communicate withthe recovery team?
What did NASA and a partner company developafter the accident?
How long did it take for the wireless headset tobe introduced to the world?
How are modern wireless headsets differentfrom the original ones?

Today’s water purifier also originated from space
technology. ⓐWhile planning their human space
exploration program, NASA scientists realized that it
was (A)[impossible / possible] to load a sufficient
amount of clean water into a spacecraft. Then, ⓑthey
hit upon an idea that wastewater could be recycled
once harmful bacteria were removed. So they
developed a water purification system that could
successfully kill off bacteria. Continued research led to
the invention of a better water purification system
that uses cartridges for longer missions that did not
need to be replaced frequently. This water purifying
technique was developed for several decades and
then marketed for domestic use.
ⓒAnother everyday item developed from space
technology is the air purifier. A reliable source of
food was vital for survival in space. ⓓIn order to get
fresh food, astronauts had to cultivate crops in the
spacecraft. However, there was a major obstacle.
When plants grow, ethylene gas is produced. It
(B)[accelerates / delays] the aging of plants and the
decaying of fruits. ⓔSince it was impossible to
exchange gas for clean air while in space, scientists
developed an air purification system to remove the
gas. Although the goal was to eliminate ethylene,
the system could get rid of other (C)[beneficial /
unwanted] things from the air, too. A private
company
recognized
the
potential
of
the
air
purification system and obtained a license to develop
and commercialize it.

A: Have you heard of the painting The Scream?
B: Of course. It is one of the most famous paintings
in the world.
A: (A)What do you think of it?
B: I think it’s a very powerful painting that shows
our inner anxiety.
A: I agree. Do you know that the painter himself
suffered from anxiety disorder?
B: Yes, I do. I think that’s why he was able to
capture the feeling of anxiety so well.
choices: How would you describe it?
How do you feel about it?
Why don’t you think of it?
What’s your opinion of it?
What’s your take on it?
solution: ‘What do you think of ~?’는 상대방에게 누군가나 무언가에 대한 의견이나 평가를 물을 때 쓰는 표현으로, 유사한 의미를 갖는 ‘How would you describe ~?(~을 어떻게 묘사하겠니?)’, ‘How do you feel about ~?(~대해 어떻게 느끼니?)’, ‘What’s your opinion of ~?(~대한 너의 의견은 무엇이니?)‘, ’What’s your take on ~?(~을 어떻게 받아들이고 있니?)‘, 등으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다. 그러나 ’Why don’t you think of ~?‘는 ’~하는 게 어때?‘라는 제안이나 권유의 뜻을 나타내는 표현이므로, 밑줄 친 (A) ‘그것에 대해 어떻게 생각하니?’를 ❸ ’그것에 대해 생 각해 보는 게 어때?‘로는 바꿔 쓸 수 없다.

Welcome
everyone
to
the
Norman
Rockwell
exhibition. My name is Harris Clark, and I will be
your guide today. Rockwell is one of the most
famous American press illustrators and painters of
all time. He produced hundreds of covers for
magazines. The main themes of his art (A)[includes
/ include] everyday life, social issues, and his
identity as an artist. Today, we will take a look at
the representative work of each theme. I will help
you (B)[to understand / understanding] the world of
his art better. Come this way.
Many of Rockwell’s works about everyday life are
quite tender. An example is Doctor and the Doll,
produced in 1929. The little girl, who seems to be
about four or five years old, is facing the old man
while holding up a doll. The man is wearing a
black suit, and there is a doctor’s bag under the
chair. The girl has already put the doll’s dress
under her arm because she wants to get her doll
(C)[examined / to exam] by the doctor. The doctor
is going along with her wish and is pretending to
listen to the doll’s heart. He is treating her and her
doll carefully. Doesn’t the look on her face look like
a worried mother at the hospital? Do you think the
girl really thinks the doll is sick or she is just
playing hospital with the doctor? This work ⓐ______
_______________________________________________. The girl’s
cuteness and the doctor’s kindness evoke a feeling
of warmth, bringing tender smiles to viewers’ faces.

(C)
choices: includesto understandexamined

includeunderstandingto exam

solution: (A) 동사 자리로 주어의 핵은 복수명사구 The main themes이 므로 이에 수일치한 복수동사 include가 적절하다. (B) 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하는 것을 돕다)’ 의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 목적격 보어로 동사원형 또는 to부정 사를 취하므로 help의 목적격보어로 to understand가 적절하다. (C) 동사 get은 ‘get+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하도록 하다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 동사 get의 목적어인 her doll과 목적격 보어는 수동 의 관계에서 목적격 보어로 과거분사를 쓰므로 examined가 적절하다.

Let’s move on to the next one. Rockwell also
produced works about the social issues of the times
he was living in. Let’s take a look at this piece. This
was painted in 1964. (A)길을 따라 한 작은 흑인 여
자아이가 순백색의 원피스를 입고, 완장을 찬 사람들
의 보호를 받으며 걸어간다. A tomato, perhaps
thrown at her, is smashed on the ground while
juice ⓐstains the wall above. The redness of the
tomato easily ⓑcaptures the viewers’ attention. The
title of this work is The Problem We All Live With.
Can you guess what contemporary issue the artist
wanted to describe? It is segregation and racism in
the U.S. This work was ⓒinspired by Ruby Bridges’
historic walk. Ruby was the first African American
child to enter an elementary school for white
children in New Orleans. The U.S. Supreme Court had
just ⓓruled the segregation of public schools for
white
and
African
American
students
to
be
unconstitutional. On her first day of school, she
walked past an angry crowd ⓔprotesting her
enrollment at the school for white students. The
historical
background
made
this
painting
an
important symbol of the Civil Rights Movement in
the U.S.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ stain: to leave a mark that is difficult to remove,especially on clothes or surfaces
ⓑ capture: to attract and hold someone’s attentionor interest
ⓒ inspire: to give someone the desire, confidence,or enthusiasm to do something or tocreate something
ⓓ rule: to have control or power over a country,area, or group of people
ⓔ protest: to express strong disagreement ordisapproval about something, especiallypublicly
solution: rule은 ‘판결을 내리다’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으나 ‘나라, 지역, 또는 사람들 집단을 지배하거나 통치하다’는 rule의 또 다른 뜻인 ‘지배하다’에 대한 영영풀이이므로, ‘to make official decisions as a leader or judge (지도자나 판사로서 공식적인 결정을 내 리다)’와 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.
